title: From synchronized embedded resolution to intrinsic smooth comparison on embeddable schemes
statement:
Fix a totally ordered set $L$ and a synchronized embedded resolution assignment $E$ with labels in $L$ [def-trf-labeled-embedded-resolution]. Work over $\mathbf Q$. Let $\mathcal C$ consist of the reduced finite-type schemes $X$ admitting a closed immersion into a smooth separated finite-type $\mathbf Q$-scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-proper-morphism]. This class includes all affine finite-type inputs and their finite disjoint unions.

There is an intrinsic assignment $A$ on $\mathcal C$: $A(X)$ is a finite ordinary blowup tower with a finite strictly increasing list of labels in $L$, coherent ideal centers, nonempty nowhere dense regular centers, and regular final scheme [def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule, def-nagata-global-blowup, pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-regular-scheme]. Nowhere dense means that the center's underlying closed set has empty interior. The tower for an empty or regular input has length zero. For every embedding $X\hookrightarrow P$ as above, its labeled ordinary tower, including the center ideals on its levels, is canonically identified with the strict-transform tower assigned by $E$; these identifications agree for different embeddings and satisfy the change-of-embedding cocycle.

For every smooth $h:Y\to X$ between members of $\mathcal C$, $A(Y)$ is canonically the contracted cartesian pullback of $A(X)$: at each retained label the ideal is the extended ideal [def-nagata-extended-ideal], and a label is absent exactly when that ideal is the unit ideal. All level squares over $h$ are cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product]. Labels remain in their original order. The comparison restricts to the canonical embedded comparison wherever $h$ extends to a smooth map of ambient schemes in a cartesian square of embedded pairs; in particular this holds for every open restriction [def-weil-open-immersion]. The ideals and level comparisons are determined by these restrictions, independently of standard-smooth charts and their lifts. There is no separatedness requirement on $h$ and no constant-relative-dimension requirement.

proof.text: For an affine rational input, apply the proved source theorem exists_isClosedImmersion_affineSpace_of_isAffine to its finite-type structure map. The finite affine-space projection is smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], affine hence separated and quasi-compact, and locally of finite type. Keep the input itself as the embedded closed scheme and use the identity initial isomorphism. For a finite coproduct of affine inputs, Mathlib instIsAffineSigmaObjScheme makes the canonical coproduct affine. Transport this property along the isomorphism from the supplied colimiting cofan, then apply the affine embedding construction. This also treats the empty coproduct. These two helpers are completely proved in Lean.

For each embeddable input S choose one of its permitted embeddings p. Apply [lem-trf-embedded-resolution-ordinary-tower] to E.tower(p) to obtain an ordinary tower and its identification at p. These choices are made only inside the existence proof, not in a definition of data from an unproved existence theorem.

For any other embedding q compose the chosen identification with E.intrinsic(p.iso.symm followed by q.iso). The initial identity follows by cancellation of p.iso and its inverse. Label equality and comap_comp prove the label and center fields. E.intrinsicComp, associativity and cancellation of each intermediate embedding isomorphism give the required cocycle. The helpers change_embedding and change_embedding_cocycle prove these transports in Lean.

For each smooth rational map between embeddable inputs, apply [lem-trf-intrinsic-resolution-smooth-comparison] to the two chosen ordinary towers and their identifications for all embeddings. Choose a resulting cartesian comparison and keep its supplied ambient compatibility proof.

Fill the unique field using [lem-trf-intrinsic-resolution-pullback-rigidity]. Fill ambient with the compatibility proof of the chosen comparison. Together with the proved embedding helpers and the change-of-embedding cocycle these are exactly all fields of IntrinsicResolutionOfEmbedded, so package them to obtain the unchanged conjunction.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q11-daf273e68 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: FIX for this split. I read in full the 9-step proof (no new nodes, statement unchanged), all 18 cited statements, def-trf-labeled-embedded-resolution and def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule. I compared old Steps 1-3 of the parent (Q27 report) with the new proof: each argument is carried, except one that old Step 2 had and the delivery dropped (polynomial ring standard smooth with c=0, so Spec Q[t] is smooth over Q). New Step 5 still relies on it when it says Q is smooth over Q by composition. Sources checked in the ILO PDF text: VIII 2.1.1 (only X-automorphism of a blowup is the identity; universal property), 2.1.3(ii) (strict transform = blowup), 2.1.9 (flat pullback), 2.3.11-2.3.13 (pp.93-94). Steps 1, 2 (rigidity from the uniqueness in the universal property plus principalization), 6, 7 (stated induction, ideal equality local on chart covers, labels of A(Y) inside labels of A(X)), 8 (base change of smooth is smooth, smooth implies flat, flat blowup base change, unit ideal gives the identity) and 9 are correct. Edge cases checked: empty or regular inputs, opens missing every center, non-surjective h, charts of different dimension, c=0, non-nilpotent I. Three C1 faults, repaired in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-trace-formula/lem-trf-embedded-to-intrinsic-smooth-resolution.json: (1) Step 3: smoothness of the ambient open immersion O->P, which E's smooth comparison needs, was uncited; now cites lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale and lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres. (2) Step 3: finite type of O over Q relied on an uncited composition of finite-type morphisms; now derived from quasi-compactness plus lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs, and the no-longer-cited lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type is removed. (3) Steps 4-5: the argument that P=Spec Q[t] is a smooth ambient is restored (def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra with c=0, standard-smooth-is-smooth, smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine), and Step 5 now names it in the composition. proof_deps is the union of the uses, and tool_uses are updated (the two new generic sk-thm-p1 tools are added). Advisory: the inherited statement clause about h extending to a smooth ambient map only makes sense for cartesian ambient squares; I read it that way. thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property's statement refers to itself, but its final-object clause is usable. No SGA, no duplicates.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer

lean.statement: theorem exists_intrinsic_resolution_of_embedded (L : Type w) [LinearOrder L] (E : SynchronizedEmbeddedResolution.{u, w} L) : (∀ (S : RationalResolutionInput.{u}) [IsAffine S.scheme], Nonempty (RationalResolutionEmbedding S)) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (S : Fin n → RationalResolutionInput.{u}) (_affine : ∀ i, IsAffine (S i).scheme) (T : RationalResolutionInput.{u}) (j : ∀ i, (S i).scheme ⟶ T.scheme) (_disjointUnion : IsColimit (Cofan.mk T.scheme j)), Nonempty (RationalResolutionEmbedding T)) ∧ Nonempty (IntrinsicResolutionOfEmbedded L E)

statement_change.what: The supplied embedded comparison is defined only for a cartesian square of embedded pairs. A mere smooth ambient extension does not provide one: the identity of a point embedded at the origin in A^1 and A^2 extends along the smooth projection A^2 to A^1, but the inverse image of the first point is A^1, not the second point. Specify the cartesian ambient square, as already required in E and the stage-1 reviewer advisory; the intrinsic comparison for arbitrary smooth h is unchanged.
